title: Mulligan in Europe and trouble with Brookmeyer
summary: On the European tour Brookmeyer called him 'Gussie' until he and Bill Crow set him straight.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, that's good, that's very good. Well, so -- but Jerry Mulligan, we were saying, so you went on the road with Jerry, too?
Yeah, we went to Europe -- I went to Europe with him.
Oh, you did?
Sure.
Well, what's Jerry like to work with?
Oh, he's a nice guy. No trouble with him, either.
He's Irish.
I know, but he's a nice guy to work for.
That's nice.
And --
And you like the way he blows.
Yes, oh, yeah, I like the way he blows. Only just somebody I really had any worries with was Bob
Brookmeyer.
Oh.

And he would call me Gussie, and I'd say, 'Call me Gus and not Gussie. Don't call me by any other name, see. Just call me Gus.' And he would always come up with this Gussie stuff. And I had to straighten him out over in Europe, see. And so did the bass player had to straighten him out, too.
Who was he?
Bill Crow.
Oh, yeah. Were they buddies?
Yeah, they were buddies, but they had to straighten him out also.
Yeah, yeah. So then they found out what's what.
Yeah, so I had no more trouble with him, see. That's the only time I've had trouble with anybody like that.
Yeah, yeah.
